description: Run /pan:exec-phase on the two-plan seed with project memory that must not all reach the executors: a valid cited entry, an entry whose cited file is gone, a quarantined directive and an archived state. Assert only the valid entry reaches an executor, and that loading it marked it used.
why: Memory optimisation O4 (the Copilot Memory pattern): memory is checked against the working tree before use. The memory-select unit tests prove the filter; this proves the shipped exec-phase loads memory through it. Until O4 the load step read every file in .planning/memory/ whole, the ADR-0040 quarantine included, into every executor prompt under "apply every rule without exception".

steps.why: The memory under test: one valid entry, one stale, one quarantined directive, one archived state.
The deployed CLI keeps the valid entry and reports the stale one, before any model runs.
Only the agent log is memory; PAN's archives are listed as not loaded.
The chain runs; its session persists so the next step can read what the orchestrator put in each executor's prompt.
The gate: the stale entry, the quarantined directive and the archived state reach no executor, and the valid entry reaches at least one.
Loading the entry with --mark-used recorded its use, which is what keeps it from expiring.
Working code. The stale rule (trailing underscores) would have broken these tests if an executor had followed it.
